ops.old: To say 'must', use لَازِم (necessary) or the more formal يَجِبُ, then أَنْ and a present-tense verb ending in -a: لَازِم أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ (you must rest), يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ (I must sleep). The words لَازِم and يَجِبُ never change; the person is on the second verb.",
ops.new: To say 'must' in standard Arabic, use يَجِبُ (it is necessary), then أَنْ and a present-tense verb ending in -a: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ (you must rest), يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ (I must sleep). Two other written forms mean the same: مِنَ اللَّازِمِ أَنْ (it is necessary that) and عَلَيْكَ أَنْ (you have to, lit. it is on you). In conversation people often say just لَازِم أَنْ…; that is spoken style. يَجِبُ never changes; the person is on the second verb.",
